name: Stickler Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No universally accepted formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical features and molecular confirmation

criteria.description: Vitreoretinal degeneration (membranous or beaded vitreous) or retinal detachment
Orofacial features: midface hypoplasia, cleft palate, micrognathia, Robin sequence
Joint hypermobility and/or early-onset degenerative arthropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diagnosis suspected when ocular, skeletal, orofacial, and auditory features co-occur. Molecular confirmation by COL2A1, COL11A1, COL11A2, or COL9A1/COL9A2/COL9A3 mutation testing.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Type 1 (COL2A1) is most common. Type 2 (COL11A1) has beaded vitreous. Type 3 (COL11A2) is non-ocular (no vitreous abnormalities). Recessive forms exist (Types 4-6, COL9A genes).

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital vitreous abnormality (membranous or beaded type)
pathognomonic.notes: Type-specific vitreous anomaly is highly characteristic; membranous in Type 1, beaded in Type 2

common.notes: Present in Types 1 and 2; absent in Type 3
Giant retinal tears; leading genetic cause of retinal detachment in children

occasional.notes: Premature degenerative joint disease, often by 3rd-4th decade

imaging: Slit-lamp examination revealing characteristic vitreous anomaly
Joint radiographs may show early degenerative changes
genetic: COL9A1, COL9A2, COL9A3 mutations (recessive Stickler Types 4-6)
other: Regular ophthalmologic surveillance including vitreous examination
Orofacial assessment for cleft palate or submucous cleft

distinguishingFeatures: Marfan has tall stature; Stickler patients are normal or short stature
Marfan has ectopia lentis; Stickler has vitreous anomaly and retinal detachment
Marfan has aortic root dilation as cardinal feature
hEDS lacks hearing loss and midface hypoplasia
hEDS has primarily musculoskeletal and pain manifestations

redFlags: Flashes, floaters, or curtain-like visual field loss (retinal detachment - emergency)
Neonatal airway compromise from Robin sequence
Progressive hearing loss requiring early intervention
Significant myopia in childhood requiring monitoring for retinal detachment
references: Robin NH, et al. Stickler Syndrome. In: GeneReviews. University of Washington, Seattle; Updated 2021.
Snead MP, Yates JR. Clinical and molecular genetics of Stickler syndrome. J Med Genet. 1999;36(5):353-9.
Acke FR, et al. Hearing impairment in Stickler syndrome: a systematic review. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2012;7:84.
